Description: Flowise v.1.6.2 and before allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted script sent to the /api/v1 component.
Mitigation: Upgrade to the latest version of Flowise that addresses this vulnerability. Ensure proper sanitization of input data received via the /api/v1 component. Use secure coding practices such as avoiding eval() and similar methods that execute arbitrary scripts. Implement input validation mechanisms and apply access control to API endpoints to limit exposure to unauthenticated users.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), AC-3 (Access Enforcement), SI-16 (Memory Protection)

Description: Flowise v.1.4.3 lacks sanitization in the fileName body parameter of the /api/v1/openai-assistants-file endpoint, allowing arbitrary file read. No known patches are available.
Mitigation: Restrict access to sensitive files by implementing strict input validation for the fileName parameter to prevent path traversal and unauthorized file access. Use input sanitization libraries and ensure proper access controls are in place. Consider applying application-layer whitelisting or sandboxing techniques for file handling to prevent unauthorized access to critical directories and system files. Monitor file access patterns for suspicious behavior.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), AC-3 (Access Enforcement), SC-28 (Protection of Information)

Description: Flowise v.1.4.3 has a CORS misconfiguration allowing arbitrary origins to connect to the website, potentially enabling attacks like path injection and data theft. No known patches are available.
Mitigation: Ensure proper CORS configuration by restricting allowed origins to trusted domains. Avoid using Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and instead specify trusted origins only. Additionally, implement proper authentication and authorization checks on all API endpoints, regardless of the CORS configuration. Monitor for and block suspicious cross-origin requests. Update Flowise to the latest secure version when available.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), AC-3 (Access Enforcement)

Description: Flowise v.1.4.3 contains a reflected XSS vulnerability in the /api/v1/chatflows/id endpoint. This vulnerability can allow attackers to inject JavaScript into user sessions, steal information, or create false popups. No known patches are available.
Mitigation: Implement input sanitization and output encoding to prevent malicious scripts from being injected into user sessions. Utilize frameworks and libraries that escape user inputs before rendering them on web pages. Apply Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to limit the execution of unauthorized scripts. Ensure error messages do not reflect user input in a way that allows XSS attacks. Additionally, consider enabling a Web Application Firewall (WAF) to mitigate XSS attack vectors.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: Horovod versions prior to 0.24.0 contain an insecure temporary file vulnerability.
Mitigation: Update Horovod to version 0.24.0 or later. Use secure temporary file handling techniques such as randomized filenames, proper file permissions, and avoiding world-writable directories to prevent attackers from tampering with temporary files.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-12 (Information Handling)

Description: LangChain (before v0.0.225) is vulnerable to RCE in JiraAPIWrapper, allowing arbitrary code execution through crafted inputs.
Mitigation: Apply security updates to LangChain (v0.0.225 or later). Use secure coding practices to validate all inputs and sanitize API interactions to prevent remote code execution. Implement logging and auditing to detect suspicious activities.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Description: LangChain (v0.0.171) is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution via load_prompt.
Mitigation: Update to a secure version of LangChain. Implement strict input validation and ensure that any prompt inputs are sanitized and verified before execution. Use sandboxing techniques to limit the impact of potential code execution within isolated environments.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-30 (Isolation of Services)

Description: LangChain (before v0.0.236) allows arbitrary code execution through Python code containing os.system, exec, or eval.
Mitigation: Upgrade to LangChain v0.0.236 or later. Remove the use of unsafe Python functions (os.system, exec, eval) and replace them with safer alternatives. Enforce strong input validation to mitigate arbitrary code execution risks.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SA-11 (Developer Training)

Description: LangChain (v0.0.64) is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution via PALChain, allowing an attacker to use Python exec method.
Mitigation: Apply updates to a secure version of LangChain. Limit or remove the usage of exec calls in the application, and implement strict input validation for all inputs interacting with PALChain. Monitor execution logs for suspicious behavior.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Description: LangChain (before v0.0.247) allows a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information via SQLDatabaseChain through SQL injection.
Mitigation: Upgrade LangChain to v0.0.247 or later. Sanitize and parameterize SQL queries to prevent SQL injection attacks. Use input validation to verify user inputs that interact with databases, and monitor logs for suspicious database activities.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: LangChain (v0.0.194) allows arbitrary code execution through Python exec calls in PALChain (from_math_prompt, from_colored_object_prompt).
Mitigation: Apply patches to LangChain (v0.0.194 or later). Avoid using Python exec calls in chain functions and replace them with safer alternatives. Implement input validation and limit the use of sensitive functions that may lead to arbitrary code execution.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: LangChain (v0.0.231) allows arbitrary code execution via the prompt parameter, affecting the security of the application.
Mitigation: Update LangChain to v0.0.231 or later. Implement robust input validation and filtering mechanisms to ensure that prompts do not include code that can be executed. Use secure programming practices, such as input sanitation, to prevent remote code execution.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: LangChain v.0.0.194 and earlier allows arbitrary code execution via the from_math_prompt and from_colored_object_prompt functions.
Mitigation: Update to LangChain v.0.0.195 or later. Avoid using dangerous functions like exec within prompts. Implement input validation to prevent arbitrary code execution and enforce the use of safe parsing and evaluation methods. Implement sandboxing to limit the impact of potential exploitation.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-30 (Isolation of Services)

Description: LangChain v.0.0.232 and earlier allows arbitrary code execution via crafted scripts to the PythonAstREPLTool._run component.
Mitigation: Upgrade LangChain to v.0.0.233 or later. Remove the ability for untrusted scripts to execute arbitrary code through the REPL tool. Implement strong input validation and restrict the use of unsafe Python methods. Use sandboxing to further limit the scope of execution in case of exploitation.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-30 (Isolation of Services)

Description: LangChain v.0.0.171 allows remote code execution via a JSON file to load_prompt through the use of __subclasses__ or template injection.
Mitigation: Upgrade LangChain to v.0.0.172 or later. Validate and sanitize JSON inputs to prevent template injection or access to Python classes via __subclasses__. Implement strict input validation for all user-supplied content and avoid the use of unsafe methods that may allow arbitrary code execution.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: LangChain v.0.0.245 allows arbitrary code execution via the evaluate function in the numexpr library, which can be exploited by remote attackers.
Mitigation: Update LangChain to v.0.0.246 or later. Ensure that untrusted inputs are never evaluated using the evaluate function in numexpr. Use input validation and safe execution practices to prevent code injection. Consider replacing numexpr with safer alternatives or sandboxing its execution to prevent potential misuse.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-30 (Isolation of Services)

Description: LangChain Experimental (before v.0.0.306) allows arbitrary code execution via __import__ in Python code, bypassing the fix for CVE-2023-36258.
Mitigation: Update LangChain Experimental to v.0.0.306 or later. Remove the use of unsafe Python attributes such as __import__ and sanitize all inputs to prevent arbitrary code execution. Use secure coding practices to ensure the same vulnerability is not reintroduced.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-30 (Isolation of Services)

Description: LangChain (before v.0.0.317) allows SSRF through document loaders like recursive_url_loader.py, potentially accessing internal servers and causing unauthorized network interactions.
Mitigation: Update to LangChain v.0.0.317 or later. Restrict external HTTP requests to trusted sources and use firewall rules to block access to internal networks. Implement logging and monitoring to detect unusual HTTP request patterns and mitigate SSRF risks.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Description: LangChain (v.0.0.155 and earlier) is vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, allowing the attacker to force the service to retrieve data from arbitrary URLs, enabling SSRF and potential downstream content injection.
Mitigation: Apply updates to LangChain v.0.0.156 or later. Sanitize and validate all user-supplied prompts to prevent prompt injection attacks. Use secure HTTP request methods and limit external access to approved URLs. Implement network-level protections like firewall rules to prevent SSRF.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: LangChain Experimental (before v.0.1.8) allows arbitrary code execution by bypassing CVE-2023-44467 fixes through unsafe Python attributes like __import__, __subclasses__, __builtins__, and others.
Mitigation: Upgrade to LangChain Experimental v.0.1.8 or later. Block the use of unsafe Python attributes that can lead to arbitrary code execution. Conduct a thorough security review to ensure that all previously introduced vulnerabilities are properly mitigated and that input validation is enforced throughout the codebase.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: LangChain Community (v.0.0.26 and earlier) is vulnerable to SSRF attacks via the load_local function, allowing remote attackers to manipulate requests and exploit internal systems.
Mitigation: Upgrade to LangChain Community v.0.0.27 or later. Implement input validation to prevent attackers from manipulating request parameters. Use network-level protections to block access to internal services and monitor logs for suspicious SSRF attempts. Ensure that external network requests are properly restricted and verified.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Description: LangChain (before v0.1.29) allows directory traversal through load_chain, disclosing sensitive information or allowing RCE.
Mitigation: Update to LangChain v0.1.29 or later. Ensure that directory traversal is prevented by sanitizing file paths. Use secure file handling practices to restrict user-supplied paths to specific directories. Implement access controls and input validation to prevent unauthorized access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), AC-6 (Least Privilege)

Description: Deserialization of untrusted data in MLflow platform running version 2.5.0 or newer allows a malicious LangChain AgentExecutor model to execute arbitrary code on an end user's system.
Mitigation: Upgrade to the latest version of LangChain and ensure the MLflow platform is updated to mitigate the deserialization vulnerability. Avoid using untrusted data in deserialization processes by validating or restricting the types of data that can be passed for deserialization. Use safe deserialization libraries and mechanisms like cryptographic signatures to verify the authenticity and integrity of the data being deserialized.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-16 (Memory Protection), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: LangChain's Web Research Retriever in version 0.1.5 allows SSRF by failing to restrict remote internet requests, enabling attackers to perform port scans, access local services, and potentially read cloud instance metadata. Exploiting this flaw could result in unauthorized access to sensitive data or interaction with internal services.
Mitigation: Upgrade to LangChain v.0.1.6 or later. Enforce strict access controls on outbound network requests made by the Web Research Retriever to prevent unauthorized requests to internal systems. Implement whitelisting for safe, external domains, and use firewall rules to block access to internal services from unauthorized sources. Also, monitor and log network traffic to detect and mitigate suspicious SSRF attempts.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Type of Attack: Incomplete Fix for Python REPL Access
Description: LangChain Experimental (before 0.0.61) provides Python REPL access without an opt-in step, allowing arbitrary Python code execution. This issue exists due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-27444, enabling attackers to bypass restrictions and execute arbitrary Python code.
Mitigation: Update to LangChain Experimental v.0.0.61 or later. Ensure that REPL access is restricted and opt-in measures are implemented to prevent unauthorized access. Remove or restrict the use of dangerous Python methods like eval or exec. Conduct a thorough code review to ensure that previously vulnerable sections are properly fixed and that no other bypass mechanisms exist. Implement input sanitization and sandboxing for executing untrusted code.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-30 (Isolation of Services)

Description: LangChain Experimental (v0.1.17 - v0.3.0) allows arbitrary code execution through sympy.sympify in LLMSymbolicMathChain.
Mitigation: Update to LangChain v0.0.306 or later. Replace or restrict the use of unsafe functions like sympy.sympify, and sanitize all inputs that interact with symbolic math operations to prevent arbitrary code execution.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-30 (Isolation of Services)

Description: LlamaIndex through 0.9.34 is vulnerable to SQL injection via the Text-to-SQL feature in several query engines.
Mitigation: Upgrade LlamaIndex to version 0.9.35 or later. Use prepared statements for all SQL queries and apply strict input validation to prevent SQL injection attacks. Regularly audit and test SQL-related code to detect injection vulnerabilities.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-39 (Process Isolation)

Description: A command injection vulnerability exists in the RunGptLLM class of the llama_index library, version 0.9.47, used by the RunGpt framework from JinaAI to connect to Language Learning Models (LLMs). The vulnerability arises from the improper use of the eval function, allowing a malicious or compromised LLM hosting provider to execute arbitrary commands on the client's machine. This issue was fixed in version 0.10.13. The exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to a hosting provider gaining full control over client machines.
Mitigation: Replace the eval function with safer alternatives like ast.literal_eval and restrict input commands.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Secure Coding Practices, Command Injection Prevention - Avoid using eval with untrusted input.

Description: TensorFlow is an Open Source Machine Learning Framework. An attacker can craft a TFLite model that would allow limited reads and writes outside of arrays in TFLite. This exploits missing validation in the conversion from sparse tensors to dense tensors. The fix is included in TensorFlow 2.8.0. The fix is also available in TensorFlow 2.7.1, TensorFlow 2.6.3, and TensorFlow 2.5.3. Users are advised to upgrade as soon as possible.
Mitigation: Enforce validation checks for tensor sizes during conversion from sparse to dense formats.
Source of Mitigation: CERT C Coding Standard, ARR32-C (Validate array indices) - Ensuring memory access is within bounds.

Description: MLflow prior to 1.23.1 has an insecure temporary file vulnerability, which can be exploited to modify or access files unexpectedly.
Mitigation: Upgrade MLflow to version 1.23.1 or later. Use secure temporary file handling practices by assigning random filenames, restricting file permissions, and avoiding world-writable directories.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-12 (Information Handling)

Description: MLflow versions prior to 2.2.2 are vulnerable to absolute path traversal, allowing attackers to access files outside the intended directories by manipulating the file path.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.2.2 or later. Apply input validation to sanitize and restrict file paths. Use path normalization to prevent access to files outside of allowed directories.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: MLflow versions prior to 2.2.1 are vulnerable to path traversal via crafted filenames like '..\filename', allowing access to files outside of allowed directories.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.2.1 or later. Implement input validation to restrict file paths and prevent directory traversal. Ensure file path sanitization is in place to avoid accessing sensitive or restricted files.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: MLflow versions prior to 2.3.1 are vulnerable to relative path traversal attacks, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive files.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.3.1 or later. Validate user inputs and sanitize file paths to prevent relative path traversal. Avoid directly using user-supplied data for file access without validation.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-34 (Non-Persistence)

Description: A directory traversal vulnerability in the /get-artifact API method of MLflow up to v2.0.1 allows attackers to read arbitrary files on the server.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow v2.1.0 or later. Apply input validation and path sanitization on all API parameters. Implement access controls on sensitive directories to prevent unauthorized file reads.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), AC-3 (Access Enforcement)

Description: Path Traversal: ..\filename vulnerability in MLflow prior to 2.3.1 enables directory traversal, allowing attackers to access restricted files.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.3.1 or later. Implement secure file path handling and validation techniques to prevent directory traversal. Ensure path validation prevents directory traversal sequences.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: MLflow prior to 2.5.0 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability, allowing attackers to access unauthorized system files through crafted input.
Mitigation: Update to MLflow 2.5.0 or later. Apply strict validation of file paths, ensure that the application only accesses files within authorized directories, and disable unnecessary file access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: MLflow prior to 2.6.0 is vulnerable to OS command injection via user-supplied input, potentially leading to remote code execution.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.6.0 or later. Ensure that all user inputs are sanitized to prevent OS command injection. Implement the principle of least privilege to minimize the impact of a successful command injection attack.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-39 (Process Isolation)

Description: MLFlow versions 2.8.1 and earlier allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information via crafted requests to the REST API.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.8.2 or later. Restrict access to sensitive API endpoints and implement secure API authentication and authorization mechanisms. Ensure that sensitive information is not exposed in error messages or logs.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest)

Description: MLflow prior to 2.9.2 contains a vulnerability in its template engine, allowing attackers to inject malicious elements into the template rendering process.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.9.2 or later. Apply proper neutralization techniques to template inputs, ensuring user input is safely handled within the template rendering engine. Avoid unsanitized user input in templates to prevent injection attacks.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-39 (Process Isolation)

Description: MLflow prior to 2.9.2 is vulnerable to path traversal attacks, allowing attackers to access unauthorized files.
Mitigation: Update to MLflow 2.9.2 or later. Enforce path sanitization and validation for all file operations. Prevent path traversal sequences like ..\ from being used to access unauthorized files or directories.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: Path traversal vulnerability in MLflow prior to 2.9.2 allows access to files outside authorized directories via crafted file paths.
Mitigation: Apply input validation to file paths to ensure path traversal sequences are disallowed. Upgrade to MLflow 2.9.2 or later. Regularly test the application for directory traversal vulnerabilities to ensure security.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SA-11 (Testing and Evaluation)

Description: MLflow versions prior to 2.9.2 are vulnerable to path traversal attacks via crafted filenames like ..\filename, allowing access to restricted files.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.9.2 or later. Implement path validation to restrict unauthorized file access. Prevent directory traversal sequences and test the application for similar vulnerabilities regularly.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: Path traversal vulnerability in MLflow 2.9.2 allows attackers to access arbitrary files via crafted 'artifact_location' and 'source' parameters.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.9.3 or later. Implement strict validation for user-supplied input in 'artifact_location' and 'source' parameters to prevent path traversal. Ensure proper sanitization and verification of file paths.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: A bypass of CVE-2023-6909 using the fragment part of a URL to perform path traversal and access arbitrary files on the server in MLflow 2.11.0.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.11.1 or later. Ensure comprehensive validation of all parts of a URI, including fragments, to prevent path traversal and unauthorized file access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: MLflow versions before 2.10.1 allow low-privilege users with EDIT permissions to delete artifacts, which is outside their intended privileges.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.10.1 or later. Implement proper validation and access control mechanisms for DELETE requests, ensuring that only users with sufficient privileges can perform artifact deletions. Audit and log all artifact deletion activities.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege), AC-2 (Account Management)

Description: Deserialization of untrusted data in MLflow 0.9.0 or newer allows malicious PyFunc models to execute arbitrary code when loaded by an end user.
Mitigation: Upgrade to the latest version of MLflow. Implement strict validation for deserialization of models, ensuring that only trusted sources are allowed. Enforce security controls to prevent arbitrary code execution during model loading.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: Deserialization of untrusted data in MLflow 1.24.0 or newer allows arbitrary code execution via maliciously uploaded pmdarima models.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 1.25.0 or later. Implement controls to prevent the deserialization of untrusted data, ensuring that only authenticated and trusted models are allowed to execute.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest)

Description: Deserialization of untrusted data in MLflow 1.27.0 or newer allows arbitrary code execution via maliciously crafted recipes.
Mitigation: Upgrade to the latest version of MLflow. Ensure recipes are validated and restricted to authorized users. Prevent deserialization of untrusted data by implementing proper security controls and validation on all recipes.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: Remote code execution vulnerability in MLflow versions 1.11.0 or newer, allowing maliciously crafted MLprojects to execute arbitrary code on an end user’s system.
Mitigation: Upgrade to the latest version of MLflow. Ensure MLprojects are validated and restricted to trusted users. Implement additional security mechanisms to prevent the execution of unauthorized code within the MLproject environment.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SC-39 (Process Isolation)

Description: Local File Inclusion vulnerability in MLflow allows arbitrary file reads by manipulating URI fragments in version 2.9.2. The issue was fixed in version 2.11.3.
Mitigation: Upgrade to MLflow 2.11.3 or later. Ensure URI validation includes all parts, including fragments, to prevent directory traversal or LFI attacks. Regularly test and audit file access controls to maintain security.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: A vulnerability in mlflow/mlflow version 2.11.1 allows attackers to create multiple models with the same name by exploiting URL encoding. This flaw can lead to Denial of Service (DoS) as an authenticated user might not be able to use the intended model, as it will open a different model each time. Additionally, an attacker can exploit this vulnerability to perform data model poisoning by creating a model with the same name, potentially causing an authenticated user to become a victim by using the poisoned model. The issue stems from inadequate validation of model names, allowing for the creation of models with URL-encoded names that are treated as distinct from their URL-decoded counterparts.
Mitigation: Implement strict validation of model names, including URL-decoding checks before saving models.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-7 (Information Integrity) - Protecting against manipulation of model parameters.

Description: The numpy.pad function in NumPy 1.13.1 and earlier is missing input validation. An empty list or ndarray can cause an infinite loop, allowing attackers to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) attack.
Mitigation: Implement proper input validation for data passed to numpy.pad to avoid infinite loops. Ensure boundary checking and reject malformed input.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation); OWASP Top 10, A6: Security Misconfiguration

Description: __init__.py in f2py in NumPy before 1.8.1 allows local users to write to arbitrary files via a symlink attack on a temporary file.
Mitigation: Use secure temporary file creation functions to avoid symlink attacks. Implement file integrity checks before file access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-3 (Access Control); OWASP A9: Using Components with Known Vulnerabilities

Description: Various test files in NumPy before 1.8.1 allow local users to write to arbitrary files via symlink attacks on temporary files.
Mitigation: Use secure methods for handling temporary files to avoid symlink attacks. Implement file access controls and restrict user permissions.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-12 (Cryptographic Protection); OWASP A6: Security Misconfiguration

Description: NumPy 1.16.0 and earlier uses the pickle Python module unsafely, allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a crafted serialized object.
Mitigation: Avoid using pickle for deserialization of untrusted input. Use safer alternatives such as json or validate input before deserialization.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP A8: Insecure Deserialization; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: A Buffer Overflow vulnerability exists in NumPy 1.9.x when specifying arrays of large dimensions. This could allow a malicious user to cause a Denial of Service.
Mitigation: Validate input dimensions and limit array sizes to prevent buffer overflows. Implement boundary checking for all array operations.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation); OWASP A9: Using Components with Known Vulnerabilities

Description: Incomplete string comparison in the numpy.core component in NumPy before 1.22.0 allows attackers to trigger slightly incorrect copying by constructing specific string objects.
Mitigation: Correct input validation for string comparisons. Ensure string handling functions correctly reject malformed or unsafe inputs.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP A6: Security Misconfiguration; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: A Null Pointer Dereference vulnerability exists in numpy.sort in NumPy < 1.19, which allows attackers to conduct DoS attacks by repetitively creating sort arrays.
Mitigation: Implement proper return-value validation to prevent null pointer dereferences. Validate input data before invoking numpy.sort.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP A6: Security Misconfiguration; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-16 (Memory Protection)

Description: Buffer overflow in array_from_pyobj in NumPy < 1.19 allows attackers to conduct DoS attacks by constructing an array with negative values.
Mitigation: Ensure proper input validation to prevent negative dimension values in array construction. Implement size limits for array dimensions.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP A6: Security Misconfiguration; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: joblib v1.4.2 contains a deserialization vulnerability via the joblib.numpy_pickle::NumpyArrayWrapper().read_array() function.
Mitigation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. Use trusted sources and implement input validation to reject malformed or dangerous serialized objects.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP A8: Insecure Deserialization; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: Ollama before 0.1.29 is vulnerable to DNS rebinding, which may allow unauthorized remote access to the full API, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion or unauthorized actions.
Mitigation: Upgrade to Ollama 0.1.29 or later. Implement DNS rebinding protection by enforcing strict host validation and same-origin policies in API requests. Ensure firewall and network configurations block unauthorized access to internal services.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection)

Description: Ollama before 0.1.34 fails to validate digest formats (e.g., fewer or more than 64 hex digits), mishandling TestGetBlobsPath test cases, and potentially leading to RCE.
Mitigation: Upgrade to Ollama 0.1.34 or later. Apply strict input validation, ensuring that the SHA256 digest adheres to the required format (64 hex digits). Test input thoroughly for boundary conditions to prevent format string attacks or RCE.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SA-11 (Testing and Evaluation)

Description: Ollama before 0.1.47 is vulnerable to directory traversal when extracting ZIP files, allowing file extraction outside of the intended parent directory.
Mitigation: Upgrade to Ollama 0.1.47 or later. Restrict ZIP extraction to a secure directory and ensure files cannot escape intended directories by validating file paths before extraction. Limit permissions on files extracted from ZIP archives.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation), SC-34 (Non-Persistence)

Description: Versions of the package ONNX before 1.13.0 are vulnerable to Directory Traversal, allowing the external_data field of the tensor proto to reference files outside the model's current directory, such as "../../../etc/passwd".
Mitigation: Update to ONNX version 1.13.0 or later. Ensure file path validation for external_data to restrict access to only allowed directories. Implement secure handling of file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation) - Validate all file paths to avoid unintended access.

Description: ONNX versions before and including 1.15.0 allow directory traversal via the external_data field of the tensor proto, bypassing a patch for CVE-2022-25882.
Mitigation: Upgrade ONNX to version 1.16.0 or later. Apply validation of input paths in external_data fields to prevent directory traversal. Ensure sandboxing and path normalization to limit file access to the model's directory.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-7 (Software Security Testing), SC-30 (Isolation and Sandboxing)

Description: ONNX versions before and including 1.15.0 are vulnerable to an out-of-bounds read due to off-by-one errors in the ONNX_ASSERT and ONNX_ASSERTM functions.
Mitigation: Upgrade ONNX to version 1.16.0 or later. Ensure that boundary checking is applied to ONNX_ASSERT functions to prevent off-by-one errors.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SA-11 (Testing and Evaluation)

Description: ONNX 1.16.0 allows attackers to overwrite arbitrary files due to improper validation in download_model_with_test_data, enabling path traversal through malicious tar files.
Mitigation: Update to ONNX 1.16.0. Implement path validation and tar file extraction security measures. Apply sandboxing to limit file access. Perform input validation and restrict tar extraction to allowed directories to prevent arbitrary file overwrite.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection), SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: Pandas through 1.0.3 can unserialize and execute commands from an untrusted file via the read_pickle() function if __reduce__ makes an os.system call.
Mitigation: Disable use of read_pickle() in untrusted environments. Enforce strict input validation and secure deserialization.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation); OWASP A8: Insecure Deserialization

Description: A remote attacker can execute arbitrary code via the _is_jailbreak function in pandas-ai v0.9.1 and earlier.
Mitigation: Update to the latest version and apply secure coding practices to limit input to critical functions.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-3 (Malicious Code Protection); OWASP Top 10, A5: Broken Access Control

Description: Llama_index v0.7.13 and earlier allows arbitrary code execution through the exec parameter in the PandasQueryEngine.
Mitigation: Sanitize and validate inputs in exec calls, and avoid using dynamic execution for untrusted inputs.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation); OWASP Top 10, A1: Injection

Description: Arbitrary code execution via a crafted request to the prompt function in PandasAI v0.8.0 and earlier.
Mitigation: Patch to the latest version. Implement input validation and use secure coding to limit code execution.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Top 10, A5: Broken Access Control; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-3 (Access Enforcement)

Description: D-Tale prior to version 3.7.0 is vulnerable to remote code execution by hosting publicly.
Mitigation: Host D-Tale internally or upgrade to version 3.7.0. Disable "Custom Filter" for external hosting environments.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection); OWASP A5: Broken Access Control

Description: D-Tale prior to 3.9.0 is vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF), allowing attackers to access files on the server.
Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.9.0 or later. Disable Load From the Web functionality to limit external access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-18 (Secure Network Access); OWASP A10: Insufficient Logging & Monitoring

Description: PandasAI through 1.5.17 allows attackers to generate arbitrary Python code via the GenerateSDFPipeline function.
Mitigation: Sanitize user input and restrict code generation to verified sources. Implement user access control mechanisms.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Top 10, A6: Security Misconfiguration; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-17 (Remote Access)

Description: D-Tale prior to version 3.14.1 is vulnerable to remote code execution due to "Custom Filter" input being exposed.
Mitigation: Upgrade to D-Tale 3.14.1. Host D-Tale securely on trusted networks only.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection); OWASP A5: Broken Access Control

Description: TorchServe gRPC ports 7070 and 7071 are not bound to localhost by default, exposing them to all interfaces. This is fixed in release 0.11.0. Users should upgrade.
Mitigation: Restrict gRPC port access to localhost only by updating the configuration and applying firewall rules to limit exposure. Regularly audit network configurations.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-17(2) (Remote Access) - Limiting access to trusted network interfaces.

Description: TorchServe allowed_urls check can be bypassed with characters like "..", allowing models to be downloaded and referenced, bypassing security checks. Fixed in release 0.11.0.
Mitigation: Implement strict URL validation and sanitization. Use secure coding practices to ensure that only validated URLs are allowed, and monitor logs for attempted bypasses.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Top 10, A5: Broken Access Control - Ensuring proper validation of user inputs.

Description: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in PyTorch before v2.2.0 via the flatbuffer_loader.cpp component.
Mitigation: Validate input sizes and bounds before processing. Implement bounds checking in the code to prevent out-of-bounds access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Information Input Validation) - Input validation to ensure data conforms to expected ranges.

Description: Use-after-free vulnerability in PyTorch before v2.2.0 in interpreter.cpp.
Mitigation: Use memory management best practices, such as proper deallocation. Conduct static analysis to detect and prevent use-after-free errors.
Source of Mitigation: CERT C Coding Standard, MSC37-C (Ensure that object lifetimes are managed correctly) - Avoiding use-after-free vulnerabilities.

Description: Heap buffer overflow in PyTorch before v2.2.0 in vararg_functions.cpp, leading to potential Denial of Service (DoS).
Mitigation: Use buffer size checks to prevent overflow. Apply runtime checks and sanitize inputs to ensure buffer constraints.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-16 (Memory Protection) - Implementing safeguards against buffer overflows.

Description: TorchServe model/workflow management API allows uploading harmful archives, which can be extracted to any location within permissions. Fixed in TorchServe 0.9.0.
Mitigation: Validate file paths and use secure extraction methods to prevent path traversal. Limit extraction to specific directories.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Top 10, A6: Security Misconfiguration - Preventing directory traversal attacks.

Description: TorchServe default configuration allows third-party remote HTTP download requests, compromising system integrity. Fixed in TorchServe 0.8.2.
Mitigation: Restrict remote download capabilities and validate all incoming requests. Use access control mechanisms to limit download permissions.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-7 (Boundary Protection) - Implementing controls for network access.

Description: Unsafe use of eval in torch.jit.annotations.parse_type_line can lead to arbitrary code execution in PyTorch before trunk/89695.
Mitigation: Avoid using eval and replace it with safer parsing methods. Conduct code audits to identify and replace insecure functions.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Top 10, A1: Injection - Preventing code injection risks through secure coding practices.

Description: Code Injection vulnerability in pytorch-lightning prior to version 1.6.0.
Mitigation: Validate input and use safer methods for handling user input. Conduct regular security reviews of code handling critical operations.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Information Input Validation) - Validating all data inputs to prevent injection attacks.

Description: pytorch-lightning is vulnerable to deserialization of untrusted data, allowing arbitrary code execution.
Mitigation: Use secure deserialization libraries and ensure that input data is validated. Implement isolation for deserialization processes.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Deserialization Cheat Sheet - Guidance on preventing deserialization vulnerabilities.

Description: A vulnerability in scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer up to version 1.4.1.post1 allows unexpected storage of all tokens in the stop_words_ attribute, potentially leading to the leakage of sensitive information. Fixed in version 1.5.0.
Mitigation: Upgrade to scikit-learn version 1.5.0 and ensure sensitive data is sanitized before vectorization.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-12 (Information Management) - Ensuring secure handling of sensitive information.

Description: MLflow versions 1.23.0 or newer are vulnerable to deserialization of untrusted data, allowing a malicious LightGBM scikit-learn model to run arbitrary code on an end user's system when the model is interacted with.
Mitigation: Ensure that only trusted models are used and sanitize input data. Implement strict deserialization checks.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Secure Coding Practices, A8: Deserialization - Validating serialized data sources.

Description: MLflow versions 1.1.0 or newer allow for deserialization of untrusted data, enabling a malicious scikit-learn model to execute arbitrary code on an end user's system when interacted with.
Mitigation: Validate and restrict the deserialization process in MLflow, ensuring only trusted and verified models are allowed. Implement serialization safeguards to reject or sanitize untrusted data inputs.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Secure Coding Practices, A8: Deserialization - Validating serialized data sources to prevent RCE.

Description: Deserialization of untrusted data can occur in versions of the MLflow platform running 1.1.0 or newer, allowing a maliciously uploaded scikit-learn model to execute arbitrary code when interacted with on an end user's system.
Mitigation: Upgrade MLflow to the latest secure version and configure MLflow to only accept models from trusted repositories. Apply access control mechanisms to prevent unauthorized model uploads.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-16 (Memory Protection) - Implement controls to validate the source of serialized data.

Description: Scikit-learn (sklearn) through 0.23.0 is vulnerable to code execution when joblib.load() is used with untrusted files due to unsafe deserialization if __reduce__ calls os.system.
Mitigation: Avoid deserializing untrusted files using joblib.load(). If deserialization is necessary, validate inputs and apply sandboxing techniques. Use secure alternatives for loading data models.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-7 (Software and Information Integrity)

Description: Libsvm v324 (in Scikit-learn 0.23.2) is vulnerable to DoS via a crafted SVM model with a large value in the _n_support array, causing a segmentation fault.
Mitigation: Validate model inputs before allowing them to interact with Libsvm APIs to ensure integrity. Use secure serialization formats and conduct boundary tests to prevent segmentation faults when loading external models.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SA-15 (Development Process, Standards, and Tools)

Description: TensorFlow's array_ops.upper_bound causes a segfault when not given a rank 2 tensor. The fix is in TensorFlow 2.13 and will be backported to TensorFlow 2.12.

Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Information Input Validation) - Ensuring inputs are checked before processing.

Description: Improper buffer restrictions in Intel(R) Optimization for TensorFlow before version 2.13.0 may allow an authenticated user to potentially enable escalation of privilege via local access.

Source of Mitigation: CERT C Coding Standard, STR31-C (Guarantee that array indexes are within bounds) - Preventing buffer overflow vulnerabilities.

Description: TensorFlow versions prior to 2.11.1 are vulnerable to crashes from invalid inputs to the Convolution3DTranspose function, potentially causing DoS.

Description: Constructing a tflite model with filter_input_channel less than 1 causes a floating point exception. Fixed in version 2.12.

Description: TensorFlow's nn_ops.fractional_avg_pool_v2 requires specific values for its pooling_ratio parameter, and invalid inputs may cause crashes.

Description: RandomPoissonV2 receives invalid input causing floating point exceptions and potential DoS.

Description: BlockLSTMGradV2 does not validate inputs fully, leading to a segfault that can be used for a denial of service attack.

Description: saved_model_cli tool in TensorFlow before 2.9.0 is vulnerable to code injection, allowing reverse shell creation when using numpy expressions.

Description: The TensorKey hash function in TensorFlow 2.8.0 has incorrect logic, leading to potential memory handling errors and crashes.

Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-16 (Memory Protection) - Addressing memory handling issues.

This is the only affected version.
Mitigation: Implement thorough bounds checking in production code, not just DCHECK. Use memory safety checks to prevent out-of-bounds reads.
Source of Mitigation: CERT C Coding Standard, MEM35-C (Ensure memory operations are bounded) - Protecting against out-of-bounds access.

Description: TensorFlow allows tensors with a large number of dimensions; overflow causes CHECK-failure. Similar to CVE-2021-29584.

Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege)

Description: Unspecified vulnerability in IBM DB2 9.7's XML feature allows remote authenticated users to read arbitrary XML files, exposing sensitive data.
Mitigation: Apply IBM DB2 updates. Limit user access to XML file reading functionality and enforce strict access controls for sensitive data access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-3 (Access Enforcement)

Description: Unspecified vulnerability in IBM InfoSphere Guardium S-TAP 8.1 for DB2 on z/OS allows local users to gain privileges via unknown vectors.
Mitigation: Apply IBM patches for Guardium S-TAP. Restrict local access to sensitive components and enforce least privilege principle to minimize the risk of privilege escalation.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege)

Description: Stack-based buffer overflow in db2aud in IBM DB2 allows local users to gain privileges through unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Update to the latest DB2 version. Implement buffer overflow protection, such as stack canaries, and ensure strict memory management policies to prevent privilege escalation.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-16 (Memory Protection)

Description: SQL injection vulnerability in the DB Integration (wfqbe) extension for TYPO3 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands.
Mitigation: Update to the latest version of the wfqbe extension for TYPO3. Implement strict input validation and query parameterization to prevent SQL injection attacks.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: Vulnerability in the XSLT library of IBM DB2 and DB2 Connect allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Update DB2 and DB2 Connect to the latest versions. Restrict access to DB2's XSLT functionality and monitor for unusual activities involving XSLT requests.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-5 (Denial of Service Protection)

Description: Vulnerability in HP StoreVirtual LeftHand OS allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code through the dbd_manager component.
Mitigation: Apply HP StoreVirtual updates. Secure critical management interfaces and services by enforcing strong authentication and access controls.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-3 (Access Enforcement)

Description: XCloner Standalone 3.5 and earlier versions have multiple CSRF vulnerabilities, allowing attackers to hijack administrator sessions to change passwords and access database backups.
Mitigation: Update XCloner to the latest version. Implement anti-CSRF tokens and secure cookie attributes (HttpOnly, Secure) to prevent session hijacking.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-23 (Session Authenticity)

Description: The Data Movement implementation in IBM DB2 9.7 through FP10, 9.8 through FP5, 10.1 before FP5, and 10.5 through FP5 on Linux, UNIX, and Windows allows remote authenticated users to bypass intended access restrictions and delete table rows via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Apply patches provided by IBM to address this vulnerability. Enforce role-based access control (RBAC) for authenticated users to restrict unnecessary privilege escalation.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-5 (Separation of Duties), AC-6 (Least Privilege)

Description: The scalar-function implementation in IBM DB2 9.7 through FP10, 9.8 through FP5, 10.1 before FP5, and 10.5 through FP5 on Linux, UNIX, and Windows allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Update IBM DB2 to the latest fixed versions. Use intrusion detection systems (IDS) to monitor and block attempts to exploit vulnerabilities involving buffer overflows.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-2 (Flaw Remediation), SI-10 (Information Input Validation)

Description: Multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in PHP scripts in the management console on Symantec Web Gateway (SWG) appliances with software before 5.2.2 DB 5.0.0.1277 allow remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Apply updates provided by Symantec. Implement proper input validation and output encoding to prevent XSS vulnerabilities.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Top Ten, A7 (Cross-Site Scripting)

Description: The management console on Symantec Web Gateway (SWG) appliances with software before 5.2.2 DB 5.0.0.1277 allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary commands via vectors related to "traffic capture."
Mitigation: Ensure that SWG appliances are updated to the latest version. Apply principle of least privilege to limit the damage caused by command injection attacks.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-7 (Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity), CM-5 (Access Restrictions)

Description: The management console on Symantec Web Gateway (SWG) appliances with software before 5.2.2 DB 5.0.0.1277 allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary commands at boot time via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Update the SWG management console software to the latest version. Enable application whitelisting to restrict the execution of unauthorized commands during the boot process.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, CM-6 (Configuration Settings), CM-7 (Least Functionality)

Description: Multiple SQL injection vulnerabilities in a PHP script in the management console on Symantec Web Gateway (SWG) appliances with software before 5.2.2 DB 5.0.0.1277 allow remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary SQL commands via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Sanitize all inputs and use prepared statements to prevent SQL injection attacks. Monitor and log database access to detect any suspicious or unauthorized activities.
Source of Mitigation: OWASP Top Ten, A1 (Injection), NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-10 (Input Validation)

Description: Vulnerability in the Data Store component of Oracle Berkeley DB. Similar to CVE-2017-3604, allows unauthenticated attacker to compromise Data Store. Requires human interaction from another user.
Mitigation: Update to the latest version of Oracle Berkeley DB. Enforce strict access controls and isolate the Data Store infrastructure to prevent unauthorized access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege), SI-2 (Flaw Remediation)

Description: Vulnerability in Oracle Berkeley DB before version 6.2.32. Allows unauthenticated attackers to compromise Data Store with successful attacks leading to full control over the Data Store.
Mitigation: Ensure Oracle Berkeley DB is updated to the recommended version. Implement user monitoring and restrict permissions to minimize the impact of successful attacks.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, CM-6 (Configuration Settings), AC-3 (Access Enforcement)

Description: Vulnerability in Oracle Berkeley DB prior to 6.2.32. This flaw enables attackers to compromise the Data Store infrastructure after interacting with another authenticated user.
Mitigation: Apply security patches for Oracle Berkeley DB. Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) to prevent unauthorized access, and monitor logs for unusual activity.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, IA-2 (Identification and Authentication)

Description: Similar to other vulnerabilities in Oracle Berkeley DB prior to 6.2.32, this CVE allows attackers to exploit the Data Store infrastructure via human interaction from another user.
Mitigation: Update to the latest version of Oracle Berkeley DB. Implement least privilege principles and restrict access to critical infrastructure components.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege), CM-6 (Configuration Settings)

Description: Vulnerability in Oracle Berkeley DB prior to 6.2.32 that allows attackers to compromise the infrastructure via interaction with another person. Leads to complete takeover of the Data Store.
Mitigation: Apply Oracle patches. Implement intrusion detection systems (IDS) to monitor for unauthorized access attempts. Enforce least privilege to reduce potential attack surfaces.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-4 (Information System Monitoring), AC-6 (Least Privilege)

Description: A vulnerability affecting Oracle Berkeley DB versions prior to 6.2.32, allowing unauthenticated attackers to compromise the Data Store infrastructure. Exploiting this flaw requires human interaction from another user.
Mitigation: Update to the latest secure version of Oracle Berkeley DB. Restrict access and perform continuous security audits to minimize unauthorized access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-3 (Access Enforcement), CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring)

Description: Oracle Berkeley DB prior to 6.2.32 allows attackers to compromise the Data Store by interacting with another user. Exploitation results in complete control over Data Store operations.
Mitigation: Apply security patches and ensure that strict access control mechanisms are in place to prevent unauthorized access. Log and monitor user activities to detect anomalies in access patterns.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-3 (Access Enforcement), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Description: Difficult to exploit vulnerability in Oracle Berkeley DB allowing attackers to compromise the system with user interaction. Affected versions include those before 6.2.32.
Mitigation: Update Oracle Berkeley DB and implement access controls. Secure sensitive data and review access logs to ensure unauthorized attempts are flagged and remediated.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-4 (System Monitoring), AC-6 (Least Privilege)

Description: Vulnerability in Oracle Berkeley DB similar to CVE-2017-3604 through CVE-2017-3613. Allows attackers to compromise the Data Store infrastructure.
Mitigation: Apply security patches to affected Oracle Berkeley DB versions. Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and least privilege principles to restrict access to critical infrastructure components.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege), CM-6 (Configuration Settings)

Description: A flaw in Oracle Berkeley DB prior to 6.2.32 allows unauthenticated attackers to compromise Data Store infrastructure with human interaction from another user.
Mitigation: Regularly patch and update Oracle Berkeley DB installations. Enforce least privilege policies and continuously monitor access logs to detect unauthorized activity.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Description: Cybozu Dezie 8.0.0 to 8.1.1 allows remote attackers to bypass access restrictions and obtain arbitrary DBM files via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Update Cybozu Dezie to the latest version. Implement stronger access controls and ensure proper monitoring of access to prevent unauthorized file access.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, AC-6 (Least Privilege), SI-4 (System Monitoring)

Description: Cybozu Dezie 8.0.0 to 8.1.1 allows remote attackers to bypass access controls to delete arbitrary DBM files via unspecified vectors.
Mitigation: Apply the latest security patches for Cybozu Dezie. Ensure proper file permissions are in place to prevent unauthorized deletion of files.
Source of Mitigation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SI-2 (Flaw Remediation), AC-6 (Least Privilege)

Description: Trax Model: Deserialization of untrusted data in model handling allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.
Mitigation: Upgrade to latest version of Transformers
Source of Mitigation: NVD Link

Description: MaskFormer Model: Improper validation of user-supplied data leads to RCE through untrusted model file parsing.
Mitigation: Upgrade to latest version of Transformers
Source of Mitigation: NVD Link

Description: MobileViTV2: Unvalidated configuration file parsing allows deserialization of untrusted data, leading to RCE.
Mitigation: Upgrade to latest version of Transformers
Source of Mitigation: NVD Link
